# Migration

What to change in your app when you upgrade across a breaking release. Before 1.0.0, a breaking
change ships in a minor release (`0.6` to `0.7`), never in a patch
([Versioning](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/mola-ui-versioning--overview)). Each section below covers one such
release and lists every breaking change in it, with the pull request, who it affects and what to
do. A release with no breaking changes has no section.

A test reads `CHANGELOG.md` and fails if a release with breaking changes has no section here, or if
a breaking pull request in it is not listed. So a breaking release cannot ship without its guide.

## 0.6 to 0.7

> Not included in the Markdown version: an interactive `ReleaseStatus` block. See it on the page: https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/mola-ui-migration--overview

Five pull requests in 0.7 are breaking. The prop renames have a codemod (see
[Codemods](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/mola-ui-codemods--overview)). The rest are a dependency to install, a type
to fix where the compiler points, or a class name to search for. A class can sit in a string, a
template or a `cn()` call, where no tool can prove it is Mola's. A search you review is safer
there than a rewrite you can't.

### One prop vocabulary, and `className` on the box you see (pull request [146](https://github.com/demogar/molaui/pull/146))

`tone` now always means a status, `variant` a presentation, `kind` a category and `size` the
t-shirt scale ([ADR 0010](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/decisions-0010-one-prop-vocabulary--overview)). The old names,
such as `Panel tone`, `Heading size` and `Container size`, still work, warn once in development
and go in 1.0.0. These changed at once:

- `className` goes to the control on `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `Switch`, `Select`, `Combobox`,
  `Autocomplete` and `NumberInput` when a `label` is set; to the field's box on `DatePicker`; and
  to the trigger on `DateRangePicker`. The label wrapper or outer element takes `wrapperClassName`.
  `Input` always renders its box, so its `className` is the box with or without adornments.
- The cva functions take the new keys: `panelVariants({ layer })`, `emptyStateVariants({ kind })`,
  `containerVariants({ width })`, `headingVariants({ visualLevel })`. `dialogPopupVariants` is
  exported as `dialogContentVariants`.
- `NumberInput`'s DOM props go to the `<input>`. `SidebarToggle` renders one
  `<span data-slot="sidebar-toggle">` around its two buttons.
- `Breadcrumb`'s `renderLink` must return an element.

**Who it affects:** code that styled a labelled form control's wrapper through `className`, called
the cva functions with the old keys, or returned something other than an element from
`renderLink`. The deprecated props affect no one yet.

**What to do:** run the codemod for the renames from a checkout of this repository, then move any
`className` meant for a labelled control's wrapper to `wrapperClassName`.

```bash
npx tsx codemods/prop-vocabulary.ts ../your-app/src --dry   # list what would change
npx tsx codemods/prop-vocabulary.ts ../your-app/src
```

### Base UI is a peer dependency (pull request [121](https://github.com/demogar/molaui/pull/121))

`@base-ui/react` moved from a pinned dependency to a peer dependency (`^1.9.0`). With a pinned
dependency, an app on a newer 1.x got a second copy, and Mola's `DirectionProvider` stopped
reaching the components that read it.

**Who it affects:** apps installed with yarn, or with pnpm set to `auto-install-peers=false`.
npm 7 and later, and pnpm 8 and later by default, install peers for you.

**What to do:** install it beside Mola, as the install line has always said.

```bash
npm install @base-ui/react@^1.9.0
```

### NumberInput's ref and handlers reach the input (pull request [122](https://github.com/demogar/molaui/pull/122))

`ref` on `NumberInput` now resolves to the `<input>` (it was the wrapping `<div>`). `onKeyDown`,
`onKeyUp`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, the clipboard and input handlers, and `autoFocus` now go to the
input too, and are typed for it.

**Who it affects:** code that measured or focused the wrapper through the ref, or handled those
events on the wrapper.

**What to do:** the compiler points at a handler typed for a `<div>`; type it for an
`HTMLInputElement`. If you need the wrapper, put your own element around the field and use that.
Calling `.focus()` on the ref now focuses the input directly.

### Tailwind's default scales are closed, and `max-w-prose` is `max-w-reading` (pull request [123](https://github.com/demogar/molaui/pull/123))

`@demogar/mola-ui/tailwind.css` now removes Tailwind's defaults wherever Mola has its own scale
([ADR 0007](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/decisions-0007-a-closed-bridge--overview)): colours, radii, shadows, blurs,
easings, animations, line heights, letter spacing, fonts, the containers above `5xl` and the
breakpoints. `tokens/mola.tokens.json` also changed shape: it is now valid W3C Design Tokens
(2025.10).

**Who it affects:** apps that import `tailwind.css` into their own Tailwind build. In those apps,
`bg-red-500` or `shadow-lg` now produce no CSS, so the element renders unstyled rather than
failing. Apps that import the compiled `styles.css` are not affected. Figma files loaded from the
old token JSON are affected.

**What to do:** search your source for the default utilities and move each to its Mola token.

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `max-w-prose` | `max-w-reading` (the same 65ch measure) |
| `max-w-6xl`, `max-w-7xl` | `max-w-page` (1180px) or `max-w-wide` (1440px) |
| `bg-red-500`, `text-gray-600` and the rest of the default palette | a role: `bg-danger`, `text-ink-muted`, `bg-cloth-pale` |
| `shadow-lg`, `shadow-md` | `shadow-raised`, or `shadow-cut` for an edge |
| `rounded-*` | nothing: the radius is zero |
| `leading-relaxed`, `leading-normal` | `leading-body` or `leading-reading` |
| `ease-in-out`, `ease-in` | `ease-cut`, or nothing: a bare `transition` already runs on it |
| `font-sans` | `font-ui` |

```bash
grep -rnE "max-w-prose|max-w-[67]xl|shadow-(sm|md|lg|xl)|rounded-|leading-(relaxed|normal|loose)|ease-in|font-sans" src/
```

If your app needs Tailwind's defaults back, import `@demogar/mola-ui/tokens.css` instead of
`tailwind.css` and bridge only the Mola names you use. Reload `tokens/mola.tokens.json` into Tokens
Studio to pick up the new shape.

### Variant props refuse `null`, and the stylesheet is built for current browsers (pull request [128](https://github.com/demogar/molaui/pull/128))

Every props interface built from a `cva()` variant used to accept `null` (`size={null}`), which
picked no variant at all. The props now take the variant names or `undefined`. The compiled
stylesheets are also built for a stated floor (Chrome 123, Edge 123, Firefox 128 and Safari 17.5)
and no longer rewrite `light-dark()` for older browsers.

**Who it affects:** code that passed `null` to a variant prop, which is now a type error, and apps
that must support browsers older than that floor.

**What to do:** pass `undefined`, or leave the prop out, where the compiler points. For older
browsers, use the `tailwind.css` route and build for your own target. Lightning CSS lowers
`light-dark()` there. Re-theme subtrees with `data-theme`, as
[Getting started](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/mola-ui-getting-started--overview) says, so a lowered token still
changes theme.
